verses.1: He ruled for one year, and then he ruled for two years over Israel.
verses.2: Shaul chose three thousand men from Israel. These men were with Shaul in Megiddo and in Mount Ebal. Another thousand men were with Jonathan in the region of Benyamin. The rest of the people were sent to their own camps.
verses.3: And Jonathan appointed a ruler over the Philistines. The Philistines heard this, and Shaul set up a trumpet throughout the land, saying, “Let the Israelites hear!”
verses.4: And all of Israel heard that Shaul had killed the governor of Philistia. Also, Nabash of Israel was killed in Philistia. The people cried out against Shaul, saying, “May God curse him!”
verses.5: And the Philistines gathered together to fight against Israel. They had thirty thousand chariots, six thousand infantrymen, and a large army of sailors who lived by the sea. They marched forward and camped at Micmas, in front of the house of Ophan.
verses.6: And the people of Israel saw that their situation was difficult. The people rushed into the caves, into the valleys, into the rocks, into the crevices, and into the holes.
verses.7: And they crossed the Jordan, into the land of Gad and Gilead. Shaul also joined them in the battle. All the people were afraid of them.
verses.8: And it was set aside for seven days, until the time appointed came. But Shemuel did not come. Then Shemuel disappeared, and the people were scattered from their place.
verses.9: And Shaul said, “Come to me, the high places and the sacrifices.” And they came up to him.
verses.10: And it happened that he stood on top of the hill. Then Shmuel came and Shaul went out to call him, in order to bless him.
verses.11: And Shemuel said, “What have you done?” And Shaul said, “I saw that the people were destroyed from above me. But you did not come to help on the appointed days. And the Philistines gathered together from all over.”
verses.12: And he said, “Now, let the Philistines come down to me. But I will not face Jehovah’s judgment. I will resist them and climb up.”
verses.13: And Shemuel said to Shaul, “You have broken the commandments of Jehovah your God. Now, Jehovah has prepared for you a queen who will rule over Israel forever.”
verses.14: And now, your queen, you have not obeyed God’s commands. You have not done what God commanded you to do. Therefore, God will judge you for not following His laws.
verses.15: And Shemuel stood up and climbed down from the ladder to the land of Benyamin. Then he led the people who were with him, numbering about six thousand men.
verses.16: And Shaul and Jonathan, their sons, along with the people who lived with them, settled on the banks of the Jordan River. The Philistines also stayed there in Micmash.
verses.17: And the destroyer came out of the Philistine camp. Three heads were there; one head turned towards the road to Apha, towards the land of Shual.
verses.18: And one head will go along the path leading to Bet Horon. And another head will go along the border that lies above the places where the soldiers are stationed.
verses.19: And there will be no destruction in all of Israel’s land, because the Philistines said that the Israelites would be destroyed or wiped out.
verses.20: And all of Israel went down to destroy one man’s household, along with his wife, children, and livestock.
verses.21: And it would be necessary to prepare for the coming days, as well as for the other things that would happen. It was also necessary to prepare for the three days of suffering, and for the time when the Ark would be placed in its proper place.
verses.22: And on the day of battle, no weapons or armor were found in the hands of all the people. But Sha’ul and Yonatan still had weapons with them.
verses.23: And they went out from the land of Philistines to the region beyond Kemash.
